analysis.title: What Matters Today: Capex Outlook: How Much of an AI Boost?, Should We Expect More Upside Inflation Surprises?, US Vol Views
key_insights: GS expects 2027 real business fixed investment growth of 8% Q4/Q4, versus consensus of 4.2%, and 2027 real GDP growth of 2.4% Q4/Q4. Real business fixed investment grew at an 11% annualized rate in 2026Q1-Q3, and GS expects 8.4% in Q4.

AI-related hardware and IP spending is estimated to exceed $900bn annualized by end-2026 (about $800bn on hardware) and reach $1.4tn by end-2027 ($1.3tn on hardware), roughly 4% of US GDP. AI remains the dominant driver of capex growth in 2027.

GS estimates the AI impact on true GDP growth at 0.8pp in 2026 and 0.7pp in 2027, after adding back semiconductor investment and chip design service exports. Indirect effects include stock market wealth effects on consumer spending, a hit to real income from higher electricity and other prices, and limited crowding out.

Spending on IRA- and CHIPS Act-subsidized manufacturing facilities is expected to keep declining and weigh on capex. Energy investment should be a positive in 2027. Higher oil prices since the start of the Iran war have led US oil producers to raise capex, adding 0.5pp to capex growth so far this year.

September and October US inflation data surprised to the upside. Upstream price increases take 6-12 months on average to pass through fully to consumer prices, so residual pressure should continue into 1H 2027. Country team forecasts have been revised up through June 2027 versus February 2026.

Historically, monthly inflation prints surprise consensus to the upside by 5-10bp in the 3-9 months after a 10% upstream price shock. Applied to price increases since the start of the Iran War, this implies a cumulative 0.1-0.2pp upside surprise over the next 9 months, partly via a January effect. Risks to near-term inflation news are skewed to the upside.
If the upside inflation surprises materialize, they could prompt modest further tightening from major central banks in early 2027.
US investor positioning is light, with net leverage at 5-year lows per GS PB. The Panic Index is at 6.5/10, and last Thursday was the largest put volume session ever.
Fed speakers and PPI data are the near-term macro catalysts before focus shifts to NVDA earnings next week. The SPX implied move through Friday is 1.10%.

The NDX 'avg stock' 1m ATM implied vol has climbed to about 44v, but this understates the pain in AI infrastructure names. The GS AI Data Center Basket (GSTMTDAT) has realized about 80v over the last month, above its Liberation Day high.
Vol of Vol had its 2nd largest single-day increase on record last Thursday, then a top-10 single-day decline on Monday. Realized vol of VVIX has surged toward all-time highs.
The GS desk favors S&P puts with vol knock-outs and cross-asset hybrids as macro hedges, citing good savings versus vanilla hedges.
